scale.description: Candidates and voters are positioned on each axis from -2 (fully pole_a) to +2 (fully pole_b); 0 = mixed/centrist on the axis. Voter weights per axis: 0 (don't care) to 2 (care a lot). Candidate scores must carry citations and a confidence level; low-confidence scores are excluded from alignment math.

axes.title: Taxes & revenue
axes.tension: Should Washington raise more revenue from high earners and wealth to fund public services, or hold the line and cut taxes?

pole_a.label: Limit & cut taxes
pole_a.description: Oppose new taxes (income, wealth, levy-cap lifts); prioritize reducing the tax burden

pole_b.label: Tax wealth to fund services
pole_b.description: Expand progressive revenue (millionaires tax, wealth tax, cap lifts) to fund public investment

axes.salience: The single most recurrent divider: LD43 senate (wealth-tax spread), LD32, LD36 senate (repeal vs architect), LD5, every levy measure, assessor race legislative agendas

axes.title: Spending & accountability
axes.tension: Is the bigger problem that government under-invests, or that it doesn't manage and audit what it already spends?

pole_a.label: Audit & restrain
pole_a.description: Oversight, audits, performance standards, and restraint before any new spending

pole_b.label: Invest & expand
pole_b.description: Expand programs and public investment as the primary lever for outcomes

axes.salience: Differentiates WITHIN parties: KCC D8 (accountability lane vs incumbent), LD32 senate (audit homelessness spending), LD33 P2, most R challengers; measures with ratchet/flexibility concerns

axes.title: Housing affordability
axes.tension: What fixes housing costs: unleashing market supply, or public investment and tenant protections?

pole_a.label: Market supply & deregulation
pole_a.description: Streamline permitting, cut red tape, let the market build; skepticism of rent regulation

pole_b.label: Public housing & tenant protections
pole_b.description: Social housing, rent stabilization, tenant right-to-counsel, public investment

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (three distinct positions), KCC D2 (social-housing levy timing), LD43 senate (rent-stabilization stringency), LD46, LD47

axes.title: Public safety & street disorder
axes.tension: Lead with enforcement and accountability, or with prevention, treatment, and non-police response?

pole_a.label: Enforcement & accountability
pole_a.description: Police staffing, prosecuting repeat offenders, mandatory treatment, clearing encampments

pole_b.label: Prevention & services
pole_b.description: Root causes, voluntary treatment, housing-first, community/non-police responders, diversion

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (sharpest), KCC D8 (three-strikes proposal), LD5 (police chief candidate), LD47, LD30; judicial races via prosecution-vs-defense formation and bail/diversion posture

axes.title: Climate & energy
axes.tension: Press forward on climate policy even when it raises costs, or prioritize energy affordability?

pole_a.label: Energy affordability first
pole_a.description: Repeal/pare back the Climate Commitment Act and gas taxes; expand all energy sources

pole_b.label: Climate action first
pole_b.description: Defend and extend carbon pricing, clean-energy transition, climate-resilient investment

axes.salience: LD36 senate (CCA architect vs repeal), LD33 P1 (eliminate CCA plank), CD9 (Basler's affordability critique), LD45 P1

axes.title: Record vs. renewal
axes.tension: Value a proven record and institutional effectiveness, or fresh perspectives and generational change?

pole_a.label: Proven record
pole_a.description: Incumbency, seniority, bills passed, institutional relationships that deliver

pole_b.label: New voices
pole_b.description: Outsider energy, generational change, lived experience over insider tenure

axes.salience: Appears in nearly every contested race; THE axis in LD37 P1, LD11 P1, CD1, CD7, and the appointment-pipeline argument in all four Supreme Court races

axes.title: Local control vs. regional consistency
axes.tension: Should decisions (zoning, schools, services) sit with the smallest local unit, or be set regionally/statewide for consistency?

pole_a.label: Local control
pole_a.description: City/parent/district control; skepticism of state mandates and regional consolidation

pole_b.label: Regional/state standards
pole_b.description: State housing mandates, regional authorities, county-level coordination

axes.salience: LD1 P2 (GMA rollback candidates), LD33 P2 (unfunded mandates), both fire-annexation measures, Covington park district

axes.title: Money & power in politics
axes.tension: How much does independence from institutional money and structural political reform matter?

pole_a.label: Work the system
pole_a.description: Coalition-building within existing party/donor structures gets results

pole_b.label: Reform the system
pole_b.description: Refuse PAC money; term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy

axes.salience: Central for Etzkorn (CD1), Gordon, Sawant/Chaudhry (CD9), Sabio-Howell (LD43), Brown (LD37), Leritz (LD5), Jacobson (KCC D8)

axes.title: Immigration & federal enforcement
axes.tension: Constrain federal immigration enforcement and protect immigrants, or prioritize enforcement and border security?

pole_a.label: Enforcement first
pole_a.description: Secure border, support ICE cooperation, enforcement of immigration law

pole_b.label: Protect immigrants
pole_b.description: Constrain ICE (masking bans, surveillance limits), sanctuary policies, legal pathways

axes.salience: CD7 (Jayapal's signature), CD9 (abolish-ICE spread), CD8 (R field), LD32 P2 (Siddiqi), LD46 senate, LD33 P1

axes.title: Healthcare system
axes.tension: Replace private insurance with a universal public system, or strengthen and fix the current system?

pole_a.label: Strengthen current system
pole_a.description: Protect ACA/Medicaid, cap drug prices, lower premiums within existing structures

pole_b.label: Single-payer transformation
pole_b.description: Medicare for All / universal public coverage as the goal

axes.salience: CD1 (three-way split), CD7, CD9 (mechanism/urgency differences), LD5 (Warmerdam single-payer), LD1 P2

axes.title: Gender, LGBTQ+ and reproductive policy
axes.tension: Should state law protect gender identity, LGBTQ+ rights and reproductive choice broadly (in school sports, medical care and anti-discrimination law), or set traditional sex-based and pro-life limits?

pole_a.label: Traditional values
pole_a.description: Sex-based eligibility for girls' and women's sports, limits on gender-affirming care for minors, pro-life positions, narrower anti-discrimination protections

pole_b.label: Progressive social policy
pole_b.description: Trans participation in sports by gender identity, reproductive and gender-affirming care as rights, broad anti-discrimination law

Primary evidence: LD47 P2 (DEI removal vs Members of Color Caucus chair), LD45 P1, LD41 P1, LD33 P1 (three-way spread), LD12 P2, LD46 senate. Curricula and parental-rights evidence now belongs to parental-rights.

axes.title: Parents and public schools
axes.tension: Should parents have broad notification, record access and opt-out rights over what schools teach and provide, or should schools and students have discretion?

pole_a.label: Parental notification and opt-out
pole_a.description: Parents notified of and able to review curricula, materials, records and school-provided health services; broad opt-out rights

pole_b.label: School and student discretion
pole_b.description: Educators set curricula under state standards; student privacy and confidentiality in some health and counseling matters; narrower opt-outs

axes.salience: General ballot: I-1 (parental rights in schools) maps here. Applies to state legislative contests, school-district and other school-adjacent measures, and statewide initiatives; never to judicial contests. Split from social so a voter can support one of I-1 and I-638 and oppose the other.

axes.title: AI & big tech
axes.tension: Regulate AI, data centers, and tech platforms aggressively, or keep Washington innovation-friendly?

pole_a.label: Innovation-friendly
pole_a.description: Light-touch regulation; treat tech/AI growth and its energy demand as opportunity

pole_b.label: Regulate aggressively
pole_b.description: AI guardrails, data-center limits/subsidy skepticism, platform accountability, data privacy

axes.salience: The novel axis this cycle: LD46 P1 (race's flashpoint, AI-industry money contested), LD32 P1 (Noble's platform), LD32 senate, LD45 P2, CD1 (halt data centers vs nationalize AI vs opportunity)

axes.title: Foreign policy & defense
axes.tension: Reduce military spending and conditions on aid (especially to Israel), or maintain defense commitments and alliances?

pole_a.label: Maintain commitments
pole_a.description: Strong defense budget, support allies including Israel, defense-industry partnership

pole_b.label: Reduce & recondition
pole_b.description: Arms embargo/aid conditions on Israel, audit/cut the Pentagon, end forever wars

axes.salience: CD9's clearest divider (HASC ranking member vs arms-embargo challengers), CD7 (War Powers), CD1

axes.title: Judicial philosophy
axes.tension: Should judges read law strictly as written, or pragmatically interpret it to protect rights as society changes?

pole_a.label: As written
pole_a.description: Strict construction, text and original meaning, judicial restraint, depoliticize the court

pole_b.label: Pragmatic & rights-protective
pole_b.description: State constitution as rights guarantor, law meeting the community where it is, openness to reform

axes.salience: SSC Pos 3 (clearest three-way philosophy spread), Pos 1 (rights-guarantor vs as-written), Pos 5 (posture toward Blake/bail), Pos 7 (Quinn/Blake critiques); Seattle Muni Court via bail/diversion posture

candidates.name: Suzan DelBene
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2012 on the Ways and Means Committee and 2026 chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee; former Microsoft executive and state Revenue director.
highlights: Campaigns on lowering costs, a permanent expanded Child Tax Credit and having "the wealthy pay their fair share" [S1]
Introduced the CHEATERS Act in July 2026 to restore $83 billion in IRS funding aimed at high-income tax evasion [S6]
Wants to roll back Medicaid cuts, lower premiums and "rein in out-of-control ICE agents" [S1]
Supports reproductive rights and opposes a nationwide abortion ban; voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports in 2025 [S1][S15]
Said in July that "Americans should not be subsidizing" the Netanyahu government's conduct, while voting against the Massie amendment that would have cut aid [S7][S9]

taxes.basis: Says the wealthy must pay their fair share and sponsored the CHEATERS Act on high-income tax enforcement, while also seeking tax cuts for working families rather than new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Platform expands programs (permanent monthly Child Tax Credit, reversing Medicaid and food-assistance cuts, two million affordable homes) without an audit-first theme.

climate.basis: Criticizes cuts to green-energy investment, sponsored the carbon-based Clean Competition Act, and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules.

experience.basis: Fourteen years in the House on Ways and Means with an enacted bill, plus prior service as state Revenue director.

reform.basis: Chairs the DCCC, her party's national House campaign operation, and raised about $1.48 million of $3.55 million from political committees.

immigration.basis: Calls for immigration reform and reining in "out-of-control ICE agents" in her pamphlet; no sponsored immigration bills recorded in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Health agenda works within the current system: lower premiums, restore Medicaid, strengthen Medicare, and oversight of Medicare's AI claims-review program; no single-payer position.

social.basis: States strong support for reproductive rights and opposition to a national abortion ban, and voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Repeated sponsor of the Email Privacy Act and other digital-privacy bills; seeking disclosure on AI-driven Medicare claim reviews.

defense.basis: Says the U.S. should not subsidize the Netanyahu government's conduct and voted against the anti-boycott bill and FY2027 NDAA, but voted against the Massie amendment cutting aid.

candidates.name: Pramila Jayapal
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 2017 and former state senator; Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and ranking member of the House Immigration Subcommittee.
highlights: Leads the Medicare for All Act and backs an ultra-millionaire wealth tax [S1]

safety.basis: Sponsored the Housing not Handcuffs Act and a moratorium on government facial-recognition use, pointing toward non-enforcement responses.

climate.basis: Pamphlet says she works to fight climate change and is Sierra Club-endorsed; no specific 2026 climate bill recorded.

experience.basis: Ten years in the House with subcommittee ranking-member and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Says she never takes corporate PAC money and leads a congressional stock-trading ban and Supreme Court reform; FEC shows $280,500 from other political committees, so not a full pole_b case.

immigration.basis: Campaigns against 'lawless ICE and CBP actions,' sponsored the ICE Out of Our Faces and Dignity for Detained Immigrants Acts, and opposes rescissions targeting immigration services.

healthcare.basis: Leads the Medicare for All Act, framing universal healthcare as a right.

social.basis: Co-chairs the Trans Equality Task Force, sponsored a Transgender Bill of Rights resolution, and campaigns on protecting abortion rights.

tech.basis: National AI Charter Act framework (federal charters, pre-release testing, kill switch, strict liability) and a biometric-surveillance moratorium.

defense.basis: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA, for the Massie amendment to cut Israel military aid, and authored the Iran War Powers resolution.

contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Adam Smith (D), in the House since 1997 and top Democrat on Armed Services, faces Republican Doug Basler for the sixth time. Smith took 47% and Basler 22% in a primary where two left-flank challengers split much of the remainder.

candidates.name: Adam Smith
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 1997, former state senator and Seattle prosecutor; ranking member and past chair of the House Armed Services Committee.
highlights: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA in July 2026, citing its $1.6 trillion price tag and anti-LGBTQ+ floor amendments [S6][S13]
Voted to block $3.3 billion in Israel military aid while saying he still supports Israel [S7][S14]
Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains the same as wages [S8]
Supports a path to single-payer healthcare and lists protecting abortion rights as a priority [S1][S3]
Endorsed by the Seattle Times, King County Democrats, Gov. Ferguson and the State Labor Council [S4]

taxes.basis: Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains like wages, saying the ultra-wealthy pay too little; no wealth tax.

spending.basis: Platform invests in housing, job training and workforce programs and opposes domestic cuts, while citing the deficit against the defense budget increase.

safety.basis: Bills on the 988 crisis line and behavioral-health crisis care centers point toward services responses.

climate.basis: Lists protecting Puget Sound and voted against overturning EPA approval of California's at-berth emission standards.

experience.basis: In Congress since 1997, Armed Services ranking member and past chair, with enacted bills.

reform.basis: Accepts PAC money ($563,000 from other committees this cycle) and runs on broad party and union endorsements; no structural-reform planks recorded.

immigration.basis: Co-introduced bills to help immigrants enter the health-care workforce.

healthcare.basis: Repeatedly says the system should be restructured toward 'a path to a single-payer plan like Medicare for All.'

social.basis: Protecting abortion rights is a campaign priority; opposes the transgender military ban and objected to anti-LGBTQ+ NDAA amendments; endorsed by HRC PAC and Planned Parenthood.

defense.basis: Mixed: voted against the FY2027 NDAA on cost and to block $3.3B in Israel aid, and backed the Iran War Powers resolution, while stating continued support for Israel and a strong defense.

contests.race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Davina Duerr, chair of the House Local Government Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Maggie Wang; Duerr took about three quarters of the primary vote. The race contrasts Duerr's vote for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million with Wang's pledge to stop tax increases and audit state spending.

candidates.name: Davina Duerr
candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2019 and chair of the House Local Government Committee, an architect and former Bothell deputy mayor whose record centers housing supply, permitting and growth management.
highlights: Lists seven bills that became law last term, including cheaper affordable-housing construction, faster housing permits and a growth-management loophole fix [S1]
Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and co-signed a session report calling it a historic step [S3][S6]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S4]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and co-signed a session report praising it as fixing an upside-down tax code.

housing.basis: Housing record centers supply-side measures: streamlining permits, cutting permitting delays (HB 2418) and lowering construction costs, rather than tenant protections.

local-control.basis: Chairs Local Government and passed state-level rules on growth management and local permitting timelines, setting standards for cities.

climate.basis: Lists a bill phasing out super-pollutant refrigerants and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated position on carbon pricing.

experience.basis: In office since 2019, committee chair, seven bills enacted last term; opponent has never held office.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.name: Shelley Kloba
candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2017 and Vice-Chair of the House Technology, Economic Development, and Veterans Committee, focused on data privacy, AI guardrails and tax-code changes.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and calls it the start of correcting an upside-down tax code [S2][S5]
Prime sponsor of the People's Privacy Act (HB 1671) and a data-broker registry bill [S8]

spending.basis: Platform emphasizes fully funding K-12, behavioral-health access and renewable-energy investment rather than audits or restraint.

safety.basis: Highlights crisis-responder teams and crisis treatment centers law enforcement can use instead of jail or the ER.

climate.basis: Supports reducing dependence on fossil fuels, renewable-energy investment and green jobs in pamphlet and website; endorsed by Sierra Club.

experience.basis: Nine years in the House, committee vice-chair, bills enacted; opponent has never held office beyond PCO.

healthcare.basis: Says health care is 'a right, not a privilege', should never be tied to employment, and calls for 'getting rid of the middleman'; no explicit single-payer proposal.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Washington Stonewall Democrats; no statement of her own beyond protecting civil rights.

parental-rights.basis: Original sponsor of and yes vote on ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list.

tech.basis: Record centers data-privacy and AI regulation: People's Privacy Act, data-broker registry bill, AI consumer-harm work; says AI should not exploit people for profit.

candidates.name: Teresa Mosqueda
candidates.summary: Incumbent District 8 councilmember since 2024 and chair of the King County Board of Health, after about seven years on the Seattle City Council; backed by Democratic organizations and labor unions.
highlights: Pamphlet priorities: affordable housing and anti-displacement, community safety through behavioral health and gun-violence prevention, and transit, childcare and healthcare for working families [S1]

spending.basis: Platform and record center on expanding investment in housing, behavioral health, public health, childcare and transit, including a budget amendment to backfill federal housing cuts and a call to invest new revenue in the health safety net.

housing.basis: Prioritizes public investment in affordable and supportive housing and anti-displacement, and sponsored the county ban on rent price-fixing algorithms (tenant protection).

safety.basis: Frames community safety around behavioral health investment and gun-violence prevention; no enforcement-first proposals in the dossier.

climate.basis: Co-sponsored the county's Strategic Climate Action Plan update and lists green housing among her priorities; climate is not a lead campaign theme.

experience.basis: Ten years of elected legislative service (Seattle City Council, then King County Council) with enacted housing and labor legislation.

candidates.name: Colleen Melody
candidates.summary: Sitting justice since January 2026, appointed after leading the Attorney General's Civil Rights Division. She calls state law "the backbone of a lot of our rights right now" and is endorsed by every sitting justice.
highlights: On the Supreme Court since January 2026; wrote the 5-4 majority in In re Marriage of Hauk (Child Relocation Act) and joined the 6-3 majority striking the natural-gas initiative [S6][S8]
Says "State law is really the backbone of a lot of our rights right now" and names Justice Kagan as a model for attention to rulings' practical effects [S9][S10]
Also told the Seattle Times the court should "stay in its lane, and not veer into policy, unnecessarily" [S12]
Led the AG's Civil Rights Division, including the travel-ban challenge [S18]
Endorsed by all sitting justices, Governors Ferguson, Inslee and Gregoire, and the State Labor Council; first in the primary with 53.03% [S1][S14]

judicial.basis: Repeatedly frames state law and state courts as rights guarantors and cites practical effects (Kagan model); her 'stay in its lane' remark and text-based Hauk opinion keep her off the pole. Down from +2 in the primary because the refreshed record adds those moderating items.

experience.basis: Incumbent with the full institutional roster behind her, but appointed and on the bench only since January 2026 after a government litigation career; evidence unchanged in substance from the primary.

candidates.name: David Stevens
candidates.summary: Mason County Superior Court judge, elected in 2023 over an appointed incumbent, with a career spanning state, federal and international prosecution and public defense. About a decade as a Spokane County deputy prosecutor, plus federal prosecutor and public-defender roles [S1][S8]
Argues appointment of judges "leads to ideological and political decisions"; reached the bench by defeating an appointed incumbent [S1][S4][S8]
First in the primary with 35.29%; endorsed by WACOPS and recommended by the state Republican Party [S7][S8]

judicial.basis: Self-described textualist/originalist; text-and-original-meaning reading of the constitution and 'not for the courts to lead the way'; unchanged from the primary, now with more statements.

safety.basis: Documented positions against the court's juvenile-warrant, arraignment-deadline and bail-related rule changes and for failure-to-appear warrants, on a prosecution-heavy career; public-defender years keep it off -2. experience.basis: A sitting elected trial judge who campaigns as the outsider to the appointment pipeline; unchanged from the primary.

candidates.name: Michael Baumgartner
candidates.summary: First-term Republican congressman, former Spokane County Treasurer and state senator, running on tax cuts, border security and defense.
highlights: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law (H.R. 1) on passage and final concurrence [S10]
Voted for the SAVE Act and the Laken Riley Act [S11]
Backs higher military spending and cuts to social services, citing the national debt [S16]
Supports a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors [S14]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2025 H.R. 1 tax cuts, campaigns on having reduced taxes, and calls a state income tax 'terrible'.

spending.basis: Calls for curbing 'reckless government spending' and cutting social services, but backs higher defense spending, so restraint is selective.

immigration.basis: Strongly supports border security and enforcement, voted for the Laken Riley Act, and calls the crackdown 'largely successful' while criticizing some ICE operations.

social.basis: Supports and says he voted for a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors; leaves abortion law to the states.

defense.basis: Supports continuing the Iran conflict 'as long as it takes', U.S. aid to Israel, and a larger defense budget.

climate.basis: Applauded withdrawal from the Columbia Basin agreement, defends the Snake River dams, and dismisses 'environmental fads'.

tech.basis: Frames AI as a race with China and offers federal incentives for data centers, with a requirement that they pay for their power and water costs.

reform.basis: Sponsored legislation banning individual stock trading by members of Congress.

experience.basis: Incumbent congressman with prior service as county treasurer and state senator.

healthcare.basis: Official site backs a 'patient-centered' system where Americans are not 'forced to follow bureaucratic directives', working within the existing structure (rural hospital fund) [S5]; he supports the H.R. 1 Medicaid eligibility restrictions as cost-cutting [S16]. contests.race_blurb: A 2024 rematch in central Spokane: Democratic incumbent Natasha Hill, who took 64.5% in the August primary, faces Republican Tony Kiepe. Hill campaigns on the 2026 millionaires tax and housing legislation; Kiepe runs on a full state budget audit, no new taxes and more police and jail capacity.

candidates.name: Natasha Hill
candidates.summary: One-term Democratic incumbent, Vice Chair of the House Housing Committee and civil litigation attorney from Hillyard, whose record includes votes for the 2026 millionaires tax and the 2025 rent-increase limits.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and says she "led on" it [S1][S3]
Voted for the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases (EHB 1217) and has called for rent stabilization [S5][S9]
Voted for ESHB 1296 and is listed as opposing I-001 and I-638 [S4][S10]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346; independently says she led on the millionaire tax, platform calls for the wealthy to pay an equitable share, and backed keeping the capital gains tax.

spending.basis: Co-wrote an op-ed urging rejection of child-care and early-learning cuts; platform supports investment in treatment, housing and job training.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent-increase limits and called for statewide rent stabilization, while also backing supply measures such as condominium reform and land banks.

safety.basis: Says incarceration without care is not effective and supports investment in mental health, addiction treatment, housing and job training.

climate.basis: Platform supports a just transition away from fossil fuels and clean-energy investment; no specific carbon-pricing record in the dossier.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2025 with two sessions and a committee vice chair post; shorter tenure than a long-serving legislator, against a never-elected opponent.

immigration.basis: Says she supported critical protections for immigrants; co-wrote an op-ed criticizing federal prosecution of ICE-facility protesters.

social.basis: Platform pledges to champion safe access to abortion; publicly listed as opposing I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights law, and is listed as opposing I-001, which would restore it.

sources.ref: VoteWA voters' guide, Spokane County, GENERAL 2026, race 186961 (candidate statement)

candidates.name: Natalie Poulson
candidates.summary: Republican special-education teacher and former Spokane Public Schools employee, running again after losing to Ormsby in 2022, on lower taxes, spending audits, enforcement-first public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Will "stand against any form of state income tax" and wants to repeal or lower the B&O tax [S2][S6]
"Enforcement first": consequences for property crime and public drug use, involuntary treatment, treatment-first over housing-first [S3][S4]
Describes herself as pro-life and supports limits on gender-affirming care for minors [S4]

taxes.basis: Opposes any state income tax and new broad-based taxes and would repeal or lower the B&O tax, in repeated statements.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for independent audits, cutting bureaucracy and not renewing programs without results.

housing.basis: "Supply-side solutions, not more spending or mandates": cut permitting delays, fees and state construction mandates, favor market-rate housing.

safety.basis: "Enforcement first," ending catch-and-release, custody or mandatory programs for repeat offenders, involuntary treatment and treatment-first over housing-first.

climate.basis: Opposes natural-gas restrictions in new construction on cost grounds; no broader climate-policy statement.

experience.basis: Never held public office beyond precinct committee officer; runs as a non-politician seeking change after 30 years of the same representation.

local-control.basis: Advocates local control of housing decisions and wants to stop Olympia from piling on construction rules.

immigration.basis: Opposes state suits against federal immigration enforcement and sanctuary incentives; supports cooperation on serious criminals.

social.basis: Pro-life and supports parental consent and limits on irreversible gender-affirming procedures for minors, while respecting current abortion law and adult choice.

parental-rights.basis: Names parental rights as a platform plank (families, not government, make decisions for children) without specific notification or opt-out proposals.

tech.basis: Opposes broad AI regulation as harmful to innovation but would roll back data-center tax exemptions.

candidates.summary: Democratic child-care business owner and Eastern Washington liaison for Governors Inslee and Ferguson, running on cost of living, child care, education, health care and housing.

social.basis: Supports current gender-affirming-care protections and shield laws and fully supports abortion protections, in questionnaire and campaign site.

tech.basis: Supports impact assessments and audits for high-risk AI, a ban on algorithmic discrimination, data protection and tighter data-center exemptions.

candidates.name: Rob Chase
candidates.summary: Two-term State Representative and former Spokane County treasurer whose signature proposal would divide Washington into two autonomous regions.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S4][S6][S7]
Prime sponsor of HB 2085 to create autonomous Puget Sound and Columbia regions [S8]
Says human activity does not affect climate change and calls the Climate Commitment Act the most damaging tax [S9][S10]
Supported the parental-rights and girls'-sports initiatives and voted against ESHB 1296 [S5][S9]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (EHB 2081) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; pledges to lower taxes for everyone.

climate.basis: Says climate change is not human-caused, the state should not act to slow it, and the Climate Commitment Act is 'taxing the air'.

experience.basis: Two House terms and eight years as county treasurer, facing a first-time candidate.

local-control.basis: Sponsors HB 2085 to devolve state government to two autonomous regions with their own governors, judges and legislators.

social.basis: Opposes abortion except for ectopic pregnancy and supported the initiative barring athletes assigned male at birth from girls' sports; cites a perfect Family Policy Institute score.

parental-rights.basis: Supported the I-1 parental-rights initiative, voted against ESHB 1296 and for faster parent access to special-education evaluations.

tech.basis: Supports building AI data centers unless they significantly affect nearby residents.

candidates.summary: Republican former Spokane City Councilmember (2022-2025), small-business owner and pastor, running on lower taxes, public safety, treatment-first homelessness policy and parental rights.

States a 100% lifetime pro-choice record; voted against the federal girls' sports and born-alive bills [S7][S18][S19]
Voted against the final FY2026 NDAA and for cutting $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel [S22][S23]
Calls for a just transition away from fossil fuels [S5]
Refuses corporate PAC money [S6]

taxes.basis: Wants big business to pay its fair share because 'there is too much wealth in too few hands,' faults tax breaks for billionaires, and voted against H.R. 1.

spending.basis: Backs expanded ACA credits and Medicaid coverage and cites $18 million in project funding; no stated restraint planks.

safety.basis: Voted against the HALT Fentanyl Act and lists gun reform as a priority; no stated policing agenda.

climate.basis: Calls for a just transition away from fossil fuels, voted to keep California's vehicle-emission waiver, and is endorsed by LCV Action Fund.

experience.basis: First-term House incumbent with six prior years in the state Senate.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money; no broader structural-reform agenda found.

immigration.basis: Condemns ICE raids as bypassing due process, voted against the Laken Riley Act, and introduced bills limiting immigration enforcement during disasters and use of FAFSA data.

healthcare.basis: Platform centers on protecting and strengthening the ACA and Medicaid, but she calls the U.S. system 'sick care' and cites creating Washington's Universal Healthcare Commission.

social.basis: States a 100% pro-choice record, supports access to gender-affirming care, and voted against H.R. 28 and H.R. 21.

defense.basis: Voted for cutting offensive military aid to Israel, against the final FY2026 NDAA, and for Iran and Lebanon War Powers resolutions; also secures military-family and installation provisions.

contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Kim Schrier (D), a pediatrician first elected in 2018, faces Republican Spencer Meline, a Leavenworth restaurant owner in his first campaign, in a district that spans eastern King County and both sides of the Cascades. Schrier took 53% in the primary to Meline's 16%.

candidates.name: Kim Schrier
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2019 and former Issaquah pediatrician on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, seeking a fifth term.
highlights: Cites bills capping insulin costs and letting Medicare negotiate drug prices; wants Medicaid cuts and ACA premium credits reversed [S1][S3]
Introduced a bill to suspend the federal gas tax through year's end; her hydropower licensing bill became law in September 2026 [S1][S9]
Pro-choice; says she twice voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports [S4][S17]
Supports border security plus a path to citizenship and codifying DACA [S5]
Says she secured over $60 million in district projects, including body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement [S1]

taxes.basis: Proposes suspending the federal gas tax while criticizing Republican tax cuts for billionaires; no proposal for new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Highlights $60 million in district projects and wants restored Medicaid and ACA credits plus more community health centers and school-based clinics.

safety.basis: Pledges to fight any effort to defund police and funded body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement, while also backing mental-health professionals alongside police.

climate.basis: Says climate change requires immediate action and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules; also proposes a gas-tax suspension and backs hydropower and fusion.

experience.basis: Four terms in the House on Energy and Commerce, with a bill signed into law in 2026.

immigration.basis: Backs a path to citizenship and codifying DACA and says the administration is "terrorizing immigrant communities," while also calling for a secure border.

healthcare.basis: Health record and platform work within the existing system: insulin caps, Medicare drug negotiation, restoring Medicaid and ACA credits, community health centers; no single-payer position.

social.basis: Pro-choice and says she twice voted to codify Roe; voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Says she led a bill to protect children's data from Big Tech and that "we need regulations to protect people and their data."

defense.basis: Voted for H.R. 4795 barring college boycotts of Israel (most Democrats opposed) and against the Massie amendment to cut aid; voted against the FY2027 NDAA.

candidates.name: Marilyn Strickland
candidates.summary: Congresswoman since 2021, former Tacoma mayor and House Armed Services member, running on her local-project record, health-care and food-aid protections, and opposition to tariffs.
highlights: Mayor of Tacoma 2010-2017; Chief Deputy Whip and New Democrat Coalition Whip [S1][S2][S4]
Voted for the final FY2026 NDAA and against cutting military aid to Israel [S17][S18]
Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes Trump's tariffs and health-care and food-aid cuts [S1][S12]

taxes.basis: Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes tariffs; no stated plank on progressive revenue.

spending.basis: Backs preserving and expanding SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP and housing aid and touts $50 million in projects; voted for the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act.

safety.basis: Voted for the HALT Fentanyl Act and cites funding for police and firefighters; no stated enforcement or prevention agenda beyond that.

climate.basis: Works to 'boost renewable energy,' voted to keep California's vehicle-emission waiver, and is endorsed by LCV and Sierra Club.

experience.basis: In Congress since 2021 after two terms as Tacoma mayor; holds House whip and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Chief Deputy Whip, New Democrat Coalition Whip and chair of ASPIRE PAC, working through party and caucus structures.

immigration.basis: Voted against the Laken Riley Act; no further immigration statements in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Pledges to protect Medicare and make care more affordable and backs reinstating ACA subsidies, all within the current system.

social.basis: Reproductive Freedom Caucus liaison, reintroduced the Abortion is Health Care Everywhere Act, and voted against H.R. 28 and H.R. 21.

defense.basis: Voted for the FY2026 NDAA and against cutting Israel military aid and says Israel has the right to defend itself; also questioned the Iran operations and backed the Iran War Powers resolution.

candidates.name: Andrew Barkis
candidates.summary: State representative since 2016 and Lacey property-management owner, running on transportation maintenance, housing supply, and opposition to income and gas tax increases.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 tax on income over $1 million) and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S5][S8][S9]
Calls himself a vocal opponent of state income taxes and gas tax increases [S3]
Advocates more housing supply and fewer barriers to development; endorsed by realtor and rental-housing groups [S3][S4]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814 and says he opposes state income taxes and gas tax increases.

spending.basis: Emphasizes fiscally responsible budgets and fighting deficit spending that outpaces revenue.

housing.basis: Advocates increased supply and removing bureaucratic barriers, opposed frequent building-code updates; backed by real-estate and rental-housing groups.

safety.basis: Says he worked to stop shortening sentences for serious crimes and to keep accountability for registered offenders; law-enforcement endorsements.

experience.basis: In the House since 2016 and Transportation ranking member, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 and is endorsed by Human Life PAC; no campaign statement on the topic.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list and added a parental right to request charter-school enrollment; no campaign statement.

contests.office_does: The U.S. Representative for Washington's 3rd District votes on federal law, taxes, spending and oversight for Southwest Washington, including Clark County.
contests.race_blurb: Two-term Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, who often votes across party lines, faces state Senate Republican Leader John Braun in a toss-up district; they finished within 0.2 points of each other in the initial primary count, and a late-September poll had them within the margin of error. They differ most on taxes, abortion, energy and money in politics, with closer overlap on border enforcement and defense.

candidates.name: John Braun
candidates.summary: Republican state Senate leader from the 20th District, retired Navy captain and Chehalis manufacturer, running on lower taxes, border security and domestic energy.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 state tax on income over $1 million, the 2025 state tax package and the 2021 capital gains tax [S6][S7][S9]
Pledges to cut waste and lower taxes; says Olympia has "an unsustainable spending problem" [S16]
Would complete border barriers, hire more agents and tighten asylum rules [S2]
Described as a consistent anti-abortion vote in the state Senate; supports sex-based eligibility in women's sports [S15]
Endorsed by President Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson and Majority Leader Steve Scalise [S14]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2026 income tax over $1M, the 2025 tax package and the 2021 capital gains tax, and pledges to lower federal taxes.

spending.basis: Repeatedly pledges to cut waste and unnecessary spending and says a spending problem cannot be solved with new revenue.

safety.basis: 'Compassion with consequences': shut down open-air drug markets and back camping bans, paired with funding detox and mental-health beds.

climate.basis: All-of-the-above energy platform including oil and gas, and voted twice against the 2021 Climate Commitment Act.

immigration.basis: Campaign centred on border barriers, more agents, tighter asylum rules and cartel interdiction; Trump's endorsement cited his border advocacy.

defense.basis: Supports 'a lethal, modern force' and rebuilding the defense industrial base, and faults his opponent on defense funding.

social.basis: Consistent anti-abortion Senate record, says he hopes to change the state's abortion law someday, and backs sex-based eligibility in women's sports.

reform.basis: Describes governing as coalition-building within the system and takes leadership PAC money; no PAC, stock-trading or term-limit reform position found.

experience.basis: Thirteen years in the state Senate, Senate Republican Leader since 2020, former Ways and Means chair.

candidates.name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
candidates.summary: Two-term Democratic congresswoman and auto-shop co-owner from Skamania County who often crosses party lines on enforcement, energy and defense votes.
highlights: Voted against the 2025 federal tax and spending law (H.R. 1) [S5][S6]
Voted for the Laken Riley Act, the SAVE Act and the 2026 Homeland Security appropriations, each with few other Democrats [S7][S8][S9]
Pro-choice; voted against federal women's sports bills but for barring Medicaid funding of gender transition for minors [S2][S12][S17]
Voted for both recent NDAAs and for War Powers limits on the Iran war [S20][S21][S23]
Refuses corporate PAC money and introduced congressional stock-trading ban and pay-freeze bills [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2025 federal tax cuts but backs an expanded Child Tax Credit and a family-farm capital gains exemption, and has taken no stand on the state income tax.

spending.basis: Says the budget must be balanced and backs a fiscal commission and a 3%-of-GDP deficit cap, though she voted against the 2025 rescissions bill.

safety.basis: Calls for stricter punishment for drug sale and possession alongside treatment, and voted for two Republican crime bills most Democrats opposed.

climate.basis: Says climate change is man-made and backs efficiency rebates, but voted with Republicans against California's clean-car waiver and for oil, gas and LNG bills.

immigration.basis: Voted for the Laken Riley Act, SAVE Act and 2026 DHS appropriations, but against H.R. 2 (2023) and the Deporting Fraudsters Act.

healthcare.basis: Would protect Medicare and Medicaid, cut out middlemen and speed generic drugs; no single-payer position found.

defense.basis: Voted for the FY2026 and FY2027 NDAAs and Ukraine aid, while voting for War Powers resolutions to end U.S. hostilities with Iran.

social.basis: Pro-choice and voted against federal sports-eligibility and gender-care criminalization bills, but voted to bar Medicaid funding of gender transition for minors.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money, introduced stock-trading ban and pay-freeze bills, and is endorsed by End Citizens United.

experience.basis: Two-term incumbent on the House Appropriations Committee who presents herself as independent of her party.

candidates.name: Ben Christly
candidates.summary: Navy veteran, flight nurse and former small-business owner who sits on the elected Clark County Charter Review Commission, running on school funding, early learning, housing and health-care access.

spending.basis: Defines responsible budgeting as investing in schools, health care and economic opportunity, including fully funding schools and expanding early learning.

social.basis: No direct statement; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Pro-Choice Washington.

experience.basis: First legislative run; his only office is an elected seat on the county charter review commission, against a two-term incumbent.

climate.basis: Calls the clean-energy transition essential but says it must not jeopardize grid reliability or raise utility costs.

experience.basis: No legislative tenure, but a sitting city councilor since 2022 and former state commissioner, running against a first-term legislator.

candidates.name: Peter Abbarno
candidates.summary: State representative since 2021, former Centralia City Council member and Centralia attorney, running on tax relief, affordability and bringing capital-budget money to the district.
highlights: Voted no on the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 tax package; pledges 'meaningful tax relief' [S5][S6][S1]
Says he helped secure $81 million in 2025 capital-budget money for the district [S15]
Voted no on 2025 rent-increase limits and the clean-fuels expansion [S8][S11]
Voted no on both 2025 bills amending the parents' rights law [S9][S10]
Chairs Cascade PAC, which funds Republican candidates [S17]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5814, calls the income tax 'unconstitutional, unpopular, and unnecessary,' and campaigns on tax relief.

spending.basis: Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and says taxpayers should spend their own money, while touting capital-budget money won for the district.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent-increase limits (EHB 1217); no other housing statements.

safety.basis: Backs more law-enforcement funding and stronger penalties for repeat offenders, opposed 2021 police-reform bills, and voted no on the 2026 officer face-covering bill.

climate.basis: Voted against the 2025 clean-fuels changes and called 2021 climate bills including cap-and-trade job-killing, while offering amendments to redirect rather than end the program.

contests.race_blurb: Open Vancouver seat, the first in 15 years, after Rep. Sharon Wylie ran for county auditor. candidates.name: Kim D. Harless
candidates.summary: Two-term Vancouver City Council member and nonprofit policy director who co-chaired the 2021 county charter review, running on progressive revenue, tenant protections, climate action and universal healthcare.
highlights: Would defend the tax on income over $1 million and the capital gains tax and expand taxes on concentrated wealth [S2]
Wants rent stabilization with a lower cap than the 2025 law, just-cause eviction and social housing [S2]
Urges a no vote on I-1 and I-638; defends comprehensive sex education and gender-affirming care access [S2]
Backs the Washington Health Trust for a unified system covering all residents and the SAFE Act on immigration enforcement [S2]
Endorsed by The Columbian's editorial board [S6]

taxes.basis: Platform defends the tax on income over $1 million and seeks more wealth taxes; says she passed Vancouver's first B&O tax.

spending.basis: Would direct new revenue to housing, education, healthcare and the public workforce, restore child-care funding and move toward free community college.

housing.basis: Platform centers rent stabilization, tenant protections and social housing; city record also includes supply measures (MFTE expansion, removing parking minimums).

safety.basis: Favors co-responders, civilian crisis response and civilian traffic enforcement, while her city record also includes body cameras and police and fire funding measures.

climate.basis: Would defend the Climate Commitment Act and adopt a climate superfund; championed Vancouver's carbon-neutrality framework and a bulk fossil-fuel storage moratorium.

experience.basis: Two terms on the Vancouver City Council and charter review co-chair; first run for the Legislature.

reform.basis: Supports ranked choice and proportional ranked choice voting and led the charter review effort to put RCV on the ballot.

immigration.basis: Would pass the SAFE Act limiting federal immigration enforcement in sensitive places, fund deportation legal defense and lists immigrant rights as a priority.

healthcare.basis: Would champion the Washington Health Trust for a unified system covering all residents; pamphlet lists universal healthcare.

social.basis: Would protect abortion access, gender-affirming care and the shield law, opposes I-638; endorsed by Pro-Choice Washington and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Urges a no vote on I-1, saying it would force schools to out LGBTQIA+ students, and would defend comprehensive sex education; her council voted to oppose I-1.

tech.basis: Wants ratepayers protected from data-center infrastructure costs with energy and water transparency, and further limits on surveillance tools such as Flock cameras.

safety.basis: Explicitly balances law-enforcement investment and body cameras with treatment-linked shelter and root-cause approaches.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent running on his council record.

candidates.name: Emily Randall
candidates.summary: First-term congresswoman and former state senator (2019-2024) running on lower costs, health-care access, abortion rights, a clean-energy transition and oversight of the Trump administration.
highlights: Wants big business to pay its fair share and voted against H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act [S3][S17]
States a 100% lifetime pro-choice record; voted against the federal girls' sports and born-alive bills [S7][S18][S19]
Voted against the final FY2026 NDAA and for cutting $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel [S22][S23]
Calls for a just transition away from fossil fuels [S5]
Refuses corporate PAC money [S6]

taxes.basis: Wants big business to pay its fair share because 'there is too much wealth in too few hands,' faults tax breaks for billionaires, and voted against H.R. 1.

spending.basis: Backs expanded ACA credits and Medicaid coverage and cites $18 million in project funding; no stated restraint planks.

safety.basis: Voted against the HALT Fentanyl Act and lists gun reform as a priority; no stated policing agenda.

climate.basis: Calls for a just transition away from fossil fuels, voted to keep California's vehicle-emission waiver, and is endorsed by LCV Action Fund.

experience.basis: First-term House incumbent with six prior years in the state Senate.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money; no broader structural-reform agenda found.

immigration.basis: Condemns ICE raids as bypassing due process, voted against the Laken Riley Act, and introduced bills limiting immigration enforcement during disasters and use of FAFSA data.

healthcare.basis: Platform centers on protecting and strengthening the ACA and Medicaid, but she calls the U.S. system 'sick care' and cites creating Washington's Universal Healthcare Commission.

social.basis: States a 100% pro-choice record, supports access to gender-affirming care, and voted against H.R. 28 and H.R. 21.

defense.basis: Voted for cutting offensive military aid to Israel, against the final FY2026 NDAA, and for Iran and Lebanon War Powers resolutions; also secures military-family and installation provisions.

candidates.name: Tarra Simmons
candidates.summary: Attorney and former nurse in the House since 2021, now Deputy Speaker Pro Tempore, known for criminal-justice, reentry and health-care legislation; the Legislative Ethics Board fined her in 2026 and she is appealing.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and 2025 capital gains, estate and B&O tax increases [S18][S20][S22]
Authored prior-authorization, charity-care and mental health parity laws [S6]
Voted against Initiative 2081 (2024) and co-sponsored its 2025 rewrite, HB 1296 [S26][S28]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 and 2025 B&O and capital gains/estate tax increases; platform calls for asking more from those who can afford it.

spending.basis: Platform calls for more state investment in housing, schools and child care, but she backed cutting Blake legal-aid funding as wasteful during a shortfall.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent and fee increase limits, said rent prices must be stabilized, backs social housing and more public housing investment.

safety.basis: Centers treatment, reentry, root causes and police accountability; voted against I-2113 restoring police pursuits.

climate.basis: Supported the Climate Commitment Act and voted for the 2024 clean-energy transition bill; platform targets major polluters.

experience.basis: Three-term incumbent and Deputy Speaker Pro Tempore with a list of authored laws, running on 'proven leadership'.

immigration.basis: Lead sponsor of HB 2641 to bar police from hiring post-2025 ICE officers; supported immigrant worker protections.

healthcare.basis: Health agenda works within the existing system: insurer prior-authorization rules, charity care, parity and drug costs; no single-payer statement.

social.basis: Pledges to defend gender-affirming care and LGBTQIA+ protections, championed abortion-care protections, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against I-2081 and co-sponsored and voted for HB 1296, which narrowed its parental rights and added student privacy rights.

candidates.name: Deborah Krishnadasan
candidates.summary: Senator since 2025 and former Peninsula School Board president, running on lowering costs, school funding and reproductive rights.

contests.race_blurb: One-term Democratic Representative Adison Richards faces Republican David Olson, a 13-year Peninsula School Board member who led the primary. They differ most on reproductive and gender policy and spending; both opposed the 2025 B&O tax package. candidates.name: David Olson
candidates.summary: Peninsula School Board member since 2013, retired Navy officer and former public finance banker, running on lower spending, no new taxes, housing supply and parental rights.
highlights: Calls for 'no more broad-based taxes' and opposes the 2025 B&O tax package (HB 2081) [S2]
Would oppose rent caps like HB 1217 and cut red tape to build housing [S2]
Supports sex-based school sports and locker-room privacy [S2]
Would 'Defend parents' right to be informed and involved' in their child's education [S2]

taxes.basis: Criticizes passing an income tax, calls for no more broad-based taxes and votes against future tax increases.

spending.basis: Calls to reduce and cut wasteful spending and tie budgets to results.

housing.basis: Frames affordability as a supply and cost-to-build problem; opposes rent caps and supports permitting and zoning reform.

safety.basis: Calls to restore public safety and stand with law enforcement.

experience.basis: Thirteen years in elected school-board office but new to the Legislature, challenging a one-term incumbent.

local-control.basis: Calls himself a strong advocate for local control and would standardize permits with local control preserved.

social.basis: Would defend sex-based sports and locker-room privacy.

parental-rights.basis: Supports parents' right to be informed, access to curriculum information, and pushing back on policies that cut parents out of decisions.

climate.basis: All-of-the-above energy platform including oil and gas, and voted twice against the 2021 Climate Commitment Act.

immigration.basis: Campaign centred on border barriers, more agents, tighter asylum rules and cartel interdiction; Trump's endorsement cited his border advocacy.

defense.basis: Supports 'a lethal, modern force' and rebuilding the defense industrial base, and faults his opponent on defense funding.

social.basis: Consistent anti-abortion Senate record, says he hopes to change the state's abortion law someday, and backs sex-based eligibility in women's sports.

reform.basis: Describes governing as coalition-building within the system and takes leadership PAC money; no PAC, stock-trading or term-limit reform position found.

experience.basis: Thirteen years in the state Senate, Senate Republican Leader since 2020, former Ways and Means chair.

candidates.name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
candidates.summary: Two-term Democratic congresswoman and auto-shop co-owner from Skamania County who often crosses party lines on enforcement, energy and defense votes.
highlights: Voted against the 2025 federal tax and spending law (H.R. 1) [S5][S6]
Voted for the Laken Riley Act, the SAVE Act and the 2026 Homeland Security appropriations, each with few other Democrats [S7][S8][S9]
Pro-choice; voted against federal women's sports bills but for barring Medicaid funding of gender transition for minors [S2][S12][S17]
Voted for both recent NDAAs and for War Powers limits on the Iran war [S20][S21][S23]
Refuses corporate PAC money and introduced congressional stock-trading ban and pay-freeze bills [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2025 federal tax cuts but backs an expanded Child Tax Credit and a family-farm capital gains exemption, and has taken no stand on the state income tax.

spending.basis: Says the budget must be balanced and backs a fiscal commission and a 3%-of-GDP deficit cap, though she voted against the 2025 rescissions bill.

safety.basis: Calls for stricter punishment for drug sale and possession alongside treatment, and voted for two Republican crime bills most Democrats opposed.

climate.basis: Says climate change is man-made and backs efficiency rebates, but voted with Republicans against California's clean-car waiver and for oil, gas and LNG bills.

immigration.basis: Voted for the Laken Riley Act, SAVE Act and 2026 DHS appropriations, but against H.R. 2 (2023) and the Deporting Fraudsters Act.

healthcare.basis: Would protect Medicare and Medicaid, cut out middlemen and speed generic drugs; no single-payer position found.

defense.basis: Voted for the FY2026 and FY2027 NDAAs and Ukraine aid, while voting for War Powers resolutions to end U.S. hostilities with Iran.

social.basis: Pro-choice and voted against federal sports-eligibility and gender-care criminalization bills, but voted to bar Medicaid funding of gender transition for minors.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money, introduced stock-trading ban and pay-freeze bills, and is endorsed by End Citizens United.

experience.basis: Two-term incumbent on the House Appropriations Committee who presents herself as independent of her party.

candidates.name: Marilyn Strickland
candidates.summary: Congresswoman since 2021, former Tacoma mayor and House Armed Services member, running on her local-project record, health-care and food-aid protections, and opposition to tariffs.
highlights: Mayor of Tacoma 2010-2017; Chief Deputy Whip and New Democrat Coalition Whip [S1][S2][S4]
Voted for the final FY2026 NDAA and against cutting military aid to Israel [S17][S18]
Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes Trump's tariffs and health-care and food-aid cuts [S1][S12]
Voted against the federal girls' sports and born-alive bills; endorsed by Planned Parenthood [S1][S13][S14]
Voted for the HALT Fentanyl Act [S16]

taxes.basis: Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes tariffs; no stated plank on progressive revenue.

spending.basis: Backs preserving and expanding SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP and housing aid and touts $50 million in projects; voted for the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act.

safety.basis: Voted for the HALT Fentanyl Act and cites funding for police and firefighters; no stated enforcement or prevention agenda beyond that.

climate.basis: Works to 'boost renewable energy,' voted to keep California's vehicle-emission waiver, and is endorsed by LCV and Sierra Club.

experience.basis: In Congress since 2021 after two terms as Tacoma mayor; holds House whip and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Chief Deputy Whip, New Democrat Coalition Whip and chair of ASPIRE PAC, working through party and caucus structures.

immigration.basis: Voted against the Laken Riley Act; no further immigration statements in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Pledges to protect Medicare and make care more affordable and backs reinstating ACA subsidies, all within the current system.

social.basis: Reproductive Freedom Caucus liaison, reintroduced the Abortion is Health Care Everywhere Act, and voted against H.R. 28 and H.R. 21.

defense.basis: Voted for the FY2026 NDAA and against cutting Israel military aid and says Israel has the right to defend itself; also questioned the Iran operations and backed the Iran War Powers resolution.

candidates.name: Andrew Barkis
candidates.summary: State representative since 2016 and Lacey property-management owner, running on transportation maintenance, housing supply, and opposition to income and gas tax increases.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 tax on income over $1 million) and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S5][S8][S9]
Calls himself a vocal opponent of state income taxes and gas tax increases [S3]
Advocates more housing supply and fewer barriers to development; endorsed by realtor and rental-housing groups [S3][S4]
Voted against ESHB 1296 (2025) and ESSB 5599 (2023) [S10][S13]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814 and says he opposes state income taxes and gas tax increases.

spending.basis: Emphasizes fiscally responsible budgets and fighting deficit spending that outpaces revenue.

housing.basis: Advocates increased supply and removing bureaucratic barriers, opposed frequent building-code updates; backed by real-estate and rental-housing groups.

safety.basis: Says he worked to stop shortening sentences for serious crimes and to keep accountability for registered offenders; law-enforcement endorsements.

experience.basis: In the House since 2016 and Transportation ranking member, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 and is endorsed by Human Life PAC; no campaign statement on the topic.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list and added a parental right to request charter-school enrollment; no campaign statement.

climate.basis: Describes himself as "a vocal opponent of ... gas tax increases" [S3] and promotes storm-damage repair "without forcing drivers to pay higher gas taxes" [S2]; the rubric places opposition to gas taxes at climate pole_a. No statement on the Climate Commitment Act, so magnitude 1.

candidates.name: Matt Marshall
candidates.summary: First-term representative, former Eatonville school director, Army veteran and physician assistant, running against new taxes and the income tax and for parents' authority.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent and former school director, against a candidate with no elected experience.

candidates.name: Jim Walsh
candidates.summary: Aberdeen publisher first elected in 2016 and state Republican Party chair since 2023; filed the 2023 parents' bill of rights and anti-income-tax initiatives and opposes the 2026 income tax.
highlights: Voted no on ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and offered amendments to it [S7]
Filed the 2023 initiatives on parents' rights (IL-2081), income taxes (IL-2111), police pursuits and cap-and-trade repeal that were certified to the Legislature [S26]
Offered an amendment to restore parental notification rights in ESHB 1296 and voted against the bill [S8][S9]

As party chair, quoted in a release stating WAGOP supports enactment of I-645 [S23]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346 and the 2025 tax package, calls the income tax unconstitutional, and filed the 2023 no-income-tax and capital-gains repeal initiatives.

spending.basis: Calls for full audits after reported losses of state dollars, ties the income tax to spending growth, voted against the 2025-27 operating budget, and filed spending-growth-limit initiatives.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent and fee increase limits and the 2026 shelter-siting bill; no affirmative housing plan in the dossier.

safety.basis: Filed police-pursuit and hard-drug initiatives, prefiled a tougher fentanyl-sentencing bill, and opposed state decertification of elected sheriffs.

climate.basis: Voted against the clean fuels program bill and filed initiatives to repeal cap-and-trade.

experience.basis: Five-term incumbent, ranking member on Civil Rights & Judiciary, and state party chair.

local-control.basis: Opposes state removal of elected sheriffs and state limits on local shelter siting; pledges to fight 'unlawful mandates from Olympia.'

immigration.basis: Voted against limits on law enforcement face coverings; session report criticizes pushing sheriffs toward non-cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

parental-rights.basis: Filed the 2023 parents' bill of rights initiative, says parents have a right to notification about school and health information, offered a notification amendment and voted against ESHB 1296.

contests.office_does: The U.S. Representative for Washington's 4th District votes on federal law, taxes, spending and oversight for Central Washington, including all of Benton County.
contests.race_blurb: An open seat after Rep. Dan Newhouse's retirement: Trump-endorsed Republican Amanda McKinney, a Yakima County commissioner who took 34.9% in the primary, faces Democrat John Duresky, a retired Air Force major and former Hanford manager who took 29.9%. They split on immigration enforcement, energy and climate policy, health coverage, the Iran war and political reform.

candidates.name: Amanda McKinney
candidates.summary: Republican Yakima County commissioner and former mortgage banker, endorsed by President Trump, running on border enforcement, affordable energy, agriculture and water.
highlights: Supports the administration's deportations and opposes any special path to legal status [S5][S12]
Backs dams, nuclear and LNG; opposes clean-energy mandates and state fuel taxes [S1][S2][S11]
Supports keeping women's sports for biological females and protecting life from conception [S3]
Pledges to rein in federal spending; flagged over $6 million in fraudulent COVID aid claims as commissioner [S2][S3]
Endorsed by Trump, Speaker Johnson and House GOP leaders [S4]

taxes.basis: Wants Washington to rethink its fuel taxes and the Climate Commitment Act and calls gun-purchase fees taxes on rights; no federal tax plan stated.

spending.basis: Says Washington 'spends too much and delivers too little', pledges to rein in spending, and cites a county fraud-screening record.

safety.basis: Runs on law and order and dismantling fentanyl networks, and funded sheriff resources and emergency communications as commissioner.

climate.basis: Opposes clean-energy mandates and the Horse Heaven wind project, campaigned for I-2066, and blames state energy policy for prices.

experience.basis: Second-term county commissioner with state and national county-association roles; has not served in Congress.

reform.basis: Built her campaign on party-leadership endorsements, PAC contributions and over $2 million in super PAC support; states no reform agenda on money in politics.

immigration.basis: Supports deportations and border enforcement, criticizes state sanctuary law, and opposes amnesty or a special path to legal status.

social.basis: Supports sex-based eligibility in women's sports and protecting life from conception, and has aligned with ending DEI programs.

tech.basis: Frames AI as a race to win with more energy production and opposes 'heavy-handed regulation' of AI and cryptocurrency.

defense.basis: Pledges to rebuild and modernize the military and a strong national defense; says Congress has reason to keep supporting the president's actions on Iran.

sources.ref: VoteWA voters' guide, Benton County, GENERAL 2026, race 186950 (candidate statement)

Nikki Torres, who moved into the 8th after court-ordered redistricting, and Kennewick School Board President Gabe Galbraith. candidates.name: Nikki Torres
candidates.summary: Four-year 15th District state senator and Republican Deputy Floor Leader, a former Pasco council member and credit-union business lender, running in the 8th after redistricting.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and against the 2025 B&O, capital gains and services tax bills [S3][S4][S5][S6]
Voted for Initiative 2081 (2024) and against ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the parents' bill of rights [S8][S9]
Prime sponsor of the 2025 school emergency-response law and the 2026 crash-prevention-zone law [S11][S12]
Pledges full police funding and changes to the 2021 police reform laws, including vehicle pursuits [S14]
Placed first in the primary with about 52% [S19]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (ESHB 2081), capital gains/estate (ESSB 5813) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; pledges to oppose 'unfair taxes'.

spending.basis: Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and pledges conservative, responsible budgets and opposition to wasteful spending, while touting $500 million in regional capital funding.

safety.basis: Law-enforcement support is her lead accomplishment; pledges full police funding and rolling back 2021 police reform limits on pursuits; sponsored the school emergency-response law.

climate.basis: Opposes the fuel-price effect of the state carbon program and defends the Snake River dams, while saying dams and salmon recovery can coexist.

housing.basis: Voted against EHB 1217 rent-increase limits; proposes working with home builders on costs.

experience.basis: Four-year senator in caucus leadership and former city council member, facing a first-time legislative candidate.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for Initiative 2081 (unanimous in the Senate) and against ESHB 1296; no stated position on I-1.

candidates.name: Gloria Mendoza
candidates.summary: One-term State Representative, former Grandview mayor and founder of a vocational-training business, running on lower taxes, budget restraint and repeal of the Climate Commitment Act.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O, services and transportation revenue bills [S4][S5][S6][S7]

spending.basis: Says the state should keep what it has without increasing the budget, voted no on the 2025 operating budget, and pledges to stop runaway government spending.

climate.basis: Calls for repealing the Climate Commitment Act over fuel costs; voted against the 2025 clean fuels program bill.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases; blames energy policies imposed on developers for home prices.

safety.basis: Called to 'finally fund the police' and for tougher theft and fentanyl penalties; campaigns on safer streets. She voted against the 2025 public safety funding bill, which carried a local option tax (S13).

tech.basis: Undecided on data centers and open to their local benefits; voted against the 2026 bill addressing large energy use facilities.

social.basis: Voted against the 2026 bill improving access to abortion medications; statement says she defends family values.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 twice and wrote that she fought for parents' access to records, review of materials and notifications.

experience.basis: Incumbent legislator and Assistant Minority Whip with eight prior years as a Grandview council member and mayor.

candidates.name: Reedy Berg
candidates.summary: Yakima deputy mayor and Toppenish middle-school history teacher running on lower taxes, Climate Commitment Act repeal and parental rights.
highlights: Opposes the state's new income tax and proposes a 0.1% sales-tax cut [S2]
Would repeal the Climate Commitment Act [S2]
Makes parents' right to know what children are taught and what medical decisions are made his first plank [S2]

taxes.basis: Opposes the income tax and new fees and taxes, proposes a sales-tax cut, and voted against placing a city property-tax levy on the ballot.

spending.basis: Pledges to cut wasteful spending and administrative overhead; says he would have cut more rather than use one-time money on city facilities.

housing.basis: Supports permitting reform to lower housing costs and says the Housing First model is not working.

safety.basis: Backs fully funding police, opposes criminal-justice rollbacks, and would require treatment as a condition of housing assistance.

climate.basis: Would repeal the Climate Commitment Act and reduce fuel taxes and regulations on energy production.

experience.basis: Two years on the Yakima City Council and now deputy mayor, while also presenting himself as 'not a career politician'.

social.basis: Voted against a Pride Month proclamation, stating there are two genders and that science does not support expanding gender identities.

parental-rights.basis: Platform says parents have the right to know what children are taught and what medical decisions are made, and that government has overstepped.

local-control.basis: In the 2026-07-16 Herald-Republic interview he says Olympia's 'excessive taxes, regulations and mandates' stifle local schools and businesses, calls for 'local control over levies and spending priorities' and pledges to block state mandates 'that drain resources' from districts [S3]. candidates.name: Derek Sarley
candidates.summary: Walla Walla school-board member since 2015, past president of the state school directors' association and PR-firm executive, running on school funding, affordability and budget reform.

housing.basis: Wants more homes built faster with fewer outdated barriers and says the state cannot subsidize its way out of scarcity.

healthcare.basis: Focuses on cost and supply within the current system (middlemen, certificate-of-need review) rather than coverage expansion.

tech.basis: Opposes special tax breaks for data centers and wants ratepayer protections and equal environmental and water rules, while cautioning against rules that block building.

experience.basis: Ten years on a school board but new to the Legislature; asks voters to choose 'someone different.'

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates; no statement of his own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; his leadership experience is in the VFW and he lost a 2025 council bid.

contests.office_does: A U.S. Representative writes and votes on federal law and spending, oversees the executive branch, and serves constituents for a two-year term; the 2nd District covers part of Snohomish County and all of Skagit, Whatcom, Island and San Juan counties.
contests.race_blurb: Thirteen-term Democratic incumbent Rick Larsen, the lead Democrat on the Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Edwin H. Feller. The race contrasts Larsen's ICE-accountability, climate and abortion-rights positions with Feller's lower-tax, enforcement-first and sex-based Title IX platform.

candidates.name: Rick Larsen
candidates.summary: Thirteen-term incumbent and lead Democrat on the House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, running on lowering costs, health care access, ICE accountability, abortion rights and infrastructure funding.
highlights: Will not vote for full-year DHS and ICE funding without oversight; voted against the Laken Riley Act [S2][S7]
Calls health care a right and backs universal coverage, with a record of ACA and Medicare cost measures [S2]
Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act and calls climate mitigation a top priority [S2][S8]
Supports the Women's Health Protection Act and cites a 100% voting record on choice [S2]
Voted for the 2024 Israel and Ukraine security supplementals [S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Supports scrapping the cap on income subject to Social Security taxes and voted against the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act; no broader wealth-tax position stated.

spending.basis: Backs expanded child care, a $17 minimum wage, Medicare hearing benefits and infrastructure investment; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

safety.basis: On fentanyl pairs 'addiction is a disease' and prevention/recovery funding with strengthening law enforcement against traffickers.

climate.basis: Says mitigating climate change must be a top priority, supports clean energy, and voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

experience.basis: Thirteenth-term incumbent and lead Democrat on Transportation & Infrastructure, facing a first-time candidate.

immigration.basis: Conditions DHS/ICE funding on oversight, wants ICE body cameras and visible ID, supports ending family detention and private detention, and voted against the Laken Riley Act.

healthcare.basis: States universal coverage as a goal but his record and proposals work through ACA and Medicare; no single-payer proposal.

social.basis: Supports suspending the filibuster to pass the Women's Health Protection Act, cites a 100% pro-choice record, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Action Fund and Stonewall Democrats.

tech.basis: Calls for 'strong guardrails' on data centers so their power and water costs are not passed to ratepayers.

defense.basis: Voted for the 2024 Israel and Ukraine security supplementals while opposing 'reckless foreign wars.'

reform.basis: S2: has voted for legislation to 'end partisan gerrymandering, require disclosure of dark money, expand opportunities to vote' (dark-money disclosure is a named pole-B item).

sources.ref: local-voters-pamphlet page 26
